notes: All 27 relevant dragon playbooks were read. 7JaLtnvSFqM supplies only Clan Castle contents and no executable steps; it remains in sources without increasing tactical support.

No complete army repeats. Among nine counted Hydra armies, seven Dragons with five Dragon Riders and eight Dragons with five Dragon Riders tie at two videos each. Seven Dragons is the most frequent Dragon count and five Dragon Riders is the most frequent Rider count. The army uses KYxypCKWh-E's seven/five composition, spells, payload and loadouts as the complete representative; 55I-qks9qdI shares its main troop core.

KYxypCKWh-E lists three owned Sky Wagons and two donated Sky Wagons as available inventory. They are removed from the troop inventory and normalized to the one Sky Wagon actually deployed per attack. Clan Castle entries are flattened to the required shape.

Other counted Hydra cores: 47wtlBeNIPw seven Dragons/seven Riders; KHh13uguqf0 and kUuUNY_Vbvk eight/five; _sotzQjtl2A five/eight; hEw-LiuJHrM six/five; s5btI1E0LdY eight/six; twbdjMD07No seven/six. F_bsbtESUHo, PY3LIEa1Wck and doh6QR3qkAY do not state complete counts.

Dragon Rider/Inferno Dragon alternatives: 2jY5eM7an2o seven/four; Ft-oCSzVdyI eight/four; I9Efble5Nnc eight/three; Oc6yKA9PQj8 nine/four; dwCMyiEttCw eight/two; t5yxQTXbY6w eight/three; wanC6B7TJyk eight/five. VrfOSHEbg4o and vUaNIZU3eno leave counts unspecified. Some of these describe only Rider deployment, so composition membership does not increase the Inferno deployment step's support.

Mass Dragon alternatives: k4aW1ytbOZ8 states 17 Dragons, llu35f-7RFk lists nine with extensive support troops, PY3LIEa1Wck leaves the count unspecified, and Sin7pQqHJLo leaves mass-Dragon counts unspecified while suggesting ten Dragons with an unspecified number of Riders. vXLlpmek7X8 leaves Super Dragon counts unspecified.

Support counts distinct videos describing the action and tactical role, once per video, including rules and policies; it does not claim agreement on every coordinate, equipment choice or trigger approximation. Combined troop or hero deployments are split into individual executable steps. Count all consumes the selected inventory without inventing a narrated batch size.

Zero delays preserve source ordering where no interval is stated. The sources do not establish a universal gap between Duke deployment, Rocket Backpack, Queen placement, Giant Arrow and the main wave. t=0 translates an explicitly described opening.

Funnel completion has no direct trigger: the default approximates it with Queen ability completion and Duke being inside. group_inside approximates approaching the core; heavy_fire approximates entering heavy damage or becoming low on health. This can react later than advice to protect troops before damage. Main spells share coarse cues because no finer common timing is stated.

threat:main approximates an unnamed dangerous defense or pathing compartment. building:inferno cannot distinguish single-target from multi-target Infernos. Exact spell footprints, the Giant Arrow line, Rocket Backpack landing and Dark Orb direction need the source's base-specific alignment; the supplied vocabulary cannot express all of them.

The default schedules one Totem and one Freeze. No unsupported recast interval is added for the remaining spells. Earthquakes are used by the three-Earthquake variant. Other support and cleanup troops remain unscheduled where the chosen common plan has no reliable cue.

Variants requiring different troops, spells, heroes, pets or equipment require the matching source army; the required variant schema has no army override. Revenge Deck variants replace Rocket Backpack with Revenge Deck and equip Fire Heart. Inferno variants replace the Dragon component with source-counted Inferno Dragons. Super Dragon totals are unknown and must not be invented.

t5yxQTXbY6w's Duke charge uses six Invisibility Spells, Fire Heart, Electro Fangs and Spirit Fox, with Seeking Shield/Rocket Spear Royal Champion instead of the Queen. t=4 and every=10 translate its 2:56, 2:46, 2:36 attack-clock schedule on a three-minute clock. It explicitly adjusts timing under Rage or early Spirit Fox loss; those conditions lack direct triggers. Royal Champion placement at three remaining spells is example-specific; inside Royal Champion approximates her funnel being finished.

vUaNIZU3eno's charge uses five Invisibility Spells, Rocket Spear/Electro Boots Royal Champion and Fire Heart/Stun Blaster/Angry Jelly Duke. inside Royal Champion approximates Rocket Spear shots being exhausted because no ammunition trigger exists. Its four-second interval is explicit and is not assigned to k4aW1ytbOZ8 or llu35f-7RFk, whose single/double/quadruple cycles have no stated seconds. Those mass-Dragon plans start with Royal Champion and send Duke after the main push.

Repeated Ice Blocks have no shared stated interval. The Ice Block variants encode an initial damage-triggered cast; additional casts and movement between them are unscheduled. 47wtlBeNIPw instead activates Rocket Backpack seven seconds after Phoenix activates; no Phoenix trigger exists, so that timing is not converted into an invented attack-clock time.

The Flame Flinger variant's approximately 60-second lead comes only from twbdjMD07No; the other Flame Flinger sources give no number. Use that source's Fire Heart/Stun Blaster/Angry Jelly Duke and Flame Flinger inventory. Siege Barracks is an alternative machine, not an additional simultaneous deployment. The Siege Barracks variant replaces the Sky Wagon and requires that source's siege inventory and payload.

The Flame Blower variant uses PY3LIEa1Wck's Flame Blower/Rocket Backpack/Angry Jelly Duke. That source also revises its army to two Overgrowth Spells by removing one Poison and one Freeze. The repeated-Overgrowth variant needs two spells; renewal now waits for the first actual Overgrowth effect to expire.

Sin7pQqHJLo's zapquake variant needs four Earthquake and six Lightning Spells and uses Eternal Tome/Rage Gem Warden. Its Queen and Duke deployment ordering is supplied by _sotzQjtl2A because Sin7pQqHJLo narrates only their abilities. Monolith and Inferno anchors approximate its stated high-value target areas; zero-delay single casts preserve its two-plus-two Earthquake and six-Lightning counts.

Revive is carried without a dedicated Revive step in this book. The current Rust executor resolves fallen-hero unit anchors at the corpse and can spend surplus spells through fallback; that behavior does not encode a source-specific revival policy. See the Dragon review's already-known-limitations audit.

Town Hall entry is contested: KHh13uguqf0 recommends an early Town Hall entry after one failure but later succeeds through the Monolith; s5btI1E0LdY changes entry with Sweepers and hero concentrations, while wanC6B7TJyk generally finishes toward the Town Hall and defending heroes. No universal Town Hall-first rule is imposed.

Sources span TH16-TH18, and several have no fixed attacking Town Hall. The representative army comes from a TH18 link. Missing counts, unresolved names such as logger or cake, accidental casts, missed arrows and explicitly criticized ability timings are not promoted to new instructions. No recall, redeploy or manual siege-release timing is established.
Steps marked completion: true were added from the source transcripts for units the consolidated playbook never deployed (docs/playbook-completion.md, merge_completion.py).

The Ice Hound alternative preserves the hound ID and its lead dependency; Mass Dragons replaces only the Dragon/Rider deployments, so a missing Lava Hound does not by itself select mass Dragons. 55I-qks9qdI 170.6–178.3: "Using an Ice Hound" provides "more tanking early on" for Dragons/Riders.

PY3LIEa1Wck 198.5–203.2 corrects the apparent praise of the Duke shot: "I fired it a little bit too quickly." The Flame Blower variant's zero-delay placeholder is not a recommendation to fire immediately; equipment-pair prerequisites and aligned-value timing still need engine support.

PB1b: recipe selects an explicit named source/variant; an ambiguous inventory retains repair-only selection. packet preserves the input action clock, primary marks the main cohort, objective binds one building, and effect prerequisites use actual cast expiry. Source inventory/loadout and frame-verification holds remain in force. These are controller policies and synthetic regression evidence, not real-game calibration.
